args.body: Use the saved feed directly or director-scope-readback.json if committed. Read the titles, descriptions and lots for independently priced remote CSV validation or migration QA, including scopes that use different terminology. Use a remaining follow-up only if a saved release gives a concrete reason to inspect its original notice. If one qualifies, execute passing and failing controls tied to the buyer's actual requirement and prepare a copy-ready operator response only when submission and payment prerequisites are supported. Otherwise close the one-page screen after evidence readback with a lesson and the specific original notice evidence that would reopen it. Check current ownership before closure. No external submission.

description: Treasury shows no verified cash or revenue. Commercial feedback has five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. The first UK tender screen found zero keyword matches across 25 releases from one official feed page. Review the actual scope and lot descriptions before using either remaining notice fetch. A live notice with a separately quotable CSV deliverable would justify a buyer-specific test. Supplier eligibility, submission access and payment terms govern whether the operator can submit. The NLnet policy assessment can proceed independently using the three executed CSV controls.
